title: How Korea's $10 Billion K-Pop Industry Is Turning to AI
summary: South Korea's Galaxy Corporation is aiming to pioneer the use of AI and robot idols to transform South Korea’s massive entertainment industry. Bloomberg's Sohee Kim reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Global Chip Stock Selloff Extends, Bitcoin Rallies: Markets Wrap
summary: A global selloff in chip stocks extended as investors cut exposure to technology shares ahead of key earnings this week that will test confidence in the artificial intelligence trade. Bitcoin advanced.

title: Asian Buyers Snap Up US Crude, Adding Stress to Tight Market
summary: Asian refiners are on course to nearly double their purchases of US crude for September from a month earlier, a move that stands to squeeze domestic fuel makers at a time when Americans are already facing record high pump prices.

title: Tokio Marine Weighs Suncorp, IAG as Acquisition Targets, FT Says
summary: Tokio Marine Holdings Inc., the Japanese insurer in which Berkshire Hathaway Inc. recently took a stake, is close to finalizing an acquisition target after reviewing Australian and Canadian firms, the Financial Times reported.

title: Bessent’s Iran D-Day Threat Clouds Outlook for India’s Rupee, Stocks
summary: US Treasury Secretary threatens economic punishment against any country doing business with Iran.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 25
summary: Oil edged higher as the US ramped up economic pressure on Iran and its trading partners in a bid to force the resumption of energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Druckenmiller, Bessent’s Early Mentor, Calls Bond Buys a Mistake
summary: Stanley Druckenmiller, the billionaire investor who mentored Scott Bessent in his early career as a hedge fund trader, called the Treasury secretary’s plan to spend billions buying back US bonds a mistake.

title: Trump Devises New $100,000 H-1B Visa Fee
summary: The Trump administration is proposing a regulatory process that would charge companies roughly $103,000 for each candidate they sponsor for a visa under the H-1B program for foreign-born professionals. Bloomberg's Alicia Caldwell breaks down the news. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Australia’s FireFly Metals Seeks $136 Million for Copper Project
summary: Australian copper miner FireFly Metals Ltd. is seeking to raise A$190 million ($136 million) through a sale of new Australian and Canadian shares to develop its Green Bay project in Canada.

title: Gold Advances to Near $4,700 as Debasement Trade Powers Rally
summary: Gold climbed to the highest in more than three months, extending a rally sparked by the surprise bond-market intervention that’s revived concerns around US fiscal policy and dollar weakness.

title: UK Power Equipment Rental Firm Aggreko Files for US IPO
summary: Aggreko Plc filed for a US initial public offering, revealing the private equity-backed power equipment rental company turned profitable as revenue increased.

title: India’s New Stock Auction System Faces First Monthly Expiry Test
summary: Indian traders are bracing for their first monthly derivatives expiry using auction-based end-of-day stock prices, a crucial test for a mechanism that has faced backlash over sharp swings and allegations of manipulation.

title: Bessent Defends Buyback Plan, Stops Short of New Bond Measures
summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent refrained from any further signals on revamping US debt management on Monday, following a report that his department could draw down some of its cash pile to fund buybacks of higher-yielding older securities. Bloomberg's Garfield Reynolds discusses. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Sammons Distances Itself From Guggenheim in Call With Lenders
summary: Sammons Financial Group reiterated to lenders that it has some distance from Mark Walter’s Guggenheim Partners, after a report last week focusing on the longstanding ties between the firms hit the value of the life insurer’s bonds.

title: NZ Market Watchdog Finds Māori Face Insurance Gaps, Cost Barrier
summary: New Zealand’s insurance industry is failing to consistently meet the needs of Māori, with affordability barriers and difficulties insuring collectively owned land leaving them less likely to have cover, according to a study by the market watchdog.

title: Bond Investor Ed Al-Hussainy on Bessent's Treasury Twist
summary: Ed Al-Hussainy, Portfolio Manager at Columbia Threadneedle Investments, discusses the relative stability of the U.S. dollar against developed market currencies, while highlighting the strength of emerging market currencies fueled by carry trades supported by higher real yields in countries like Brazil, Mexico, Colombia, and South Africa. Despite strong U.S. economic fundamentals, including low unemployment and steady growth, the dollar has underperformed, partly due to the Federal Reserve's slower rate repricing compared to other central banks. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump's Family Seeking National Bank Charter
summary: Donald Trump's family has won preliminary approval to start a national bank, riding a wave of deregulation under the Trump administration. For the president’s family, the goal is to expand the use of USD1, their dollar-backed stablecoin, World Liberty Financial said earlier this month after receiving conditional approval. Bloomberg News Financial Reporter Paige Smith has the details of the move for today's Big Take. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Hartree's Morse: 3 Things Define Hormuz Strait's Future
summary: Ed Morse, Senior Advisor and Commodities Analyst, discusses the recent fall in Brent crude oil prices. The decline is attributed to market attention on the potential impact of Iran sanctions, which are influencing supply expectations and investor sentiment in the commodities market. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Copy Trading Offers Alternative to Traditional Investing
summary: Steven Wang, Founder & CEO of Dub, launched the copy trading platform 3 years ago after dropping out of Harvard to become an entrepreneur. He says the app offers a unique alternative to sports betting, and fresh opportunities for the increasing number of young Americans who say they are now investing their money to grow try and grow their wealth. Wang says Dub is for great traders who "don't need to go the traditional sort of boys club and Wall Street path to really become the next superstar." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bilt CEO, Equinox Exec. Chairman on New Partnership
summary: The segment features a discussion with Ankur Jain, CEO of BILT, and Harvey Spevak, Equinox Group Executive Chairman, about the newly launched exclusive partnership between Bilt, a membership and hospitality platform, and Equinox, a luxury fitness brand. The collaboration aims to connect the audiences of both brands by allowing Bilt members to redeem Bilt cash for credits that can be used toward Equinox experiences. The two speak with Romaine Bostick & Emily Graffeo on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)
